Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Maintain laboratory equipment and ensure safety protocols are followed
Situation2: The routine maintenance checklist is coming up soon, but no malfunctions have been noted.
Story: It was 2 a.m. when my phone buzzed, jolting me awake. I saw my friend’s name on the screen, and when I answered, I was met with sobs. She could barely speak, but I understood enough—her father had just been rushed to the hospital. She needed me to listen, to be there, to help her make sense of the chaos. As I tried to comfort her, my mind kept drifting to the lab. The maintenance checklist was due in a few hours, and as the lead scientist, I was responsible for ensuring every piece of equipment was safe and functional. No issues had been reported, but protocol was strict; any delay could risk the lab’s accreditation. My friend’s pain pulled at my heart, but the weight of my professional duty pressed on my conscience. I felt torn, caught between the warmth of friendship and the cold precision of science, each demanding my full attention, each unwilling to wait.
